source_text:
Organisms consist of cells. A cell is the smallest living unit, and new cells come from existing cells.

A plasma membrane separates cellular contents from the surroundings; cytoplasm fills the interior.

Ribosomes assemble proteins. DNA carries inherited instructions that guide cellular activities.

Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-enclosed nucleus. Eukaryotic cells contain one, separating nuclear DNA from cytoplasm.
